core_obligations: Given the existing general nodal-domain reduction/Weyl law,sharpHeisenberg Sobolev inputs and classical Euclidean symmetrization,one still needs quantitative constants strong enough to make the model Pleijel constant strictly less than1. The paper develops a source-specific horizontal Folland-kernel optimization over measurable sets (bathtub superlevel geometry and exactdirectional integrals) to improve the Heisenberg isoperimetric bound,then transports this bound through BV slicing/product perimeters and symmetrization to the product Faber-Krahn constant. These estimates settle the low-dimensional (n,k)=(1,2),(2,1) cases not obtained from the earlier Sobolev route,while the productSobolev/monotonicity analysis covers the remaining n>=3 cases. This non-routine quantitative subelliptic functional-inequality construction supplies one H2 strict-Pleijel theorem;it is not the alreadyqualified2367 general varying-model upperbound,an isolated multiplication of constants,or a count for every case/tool. Originalauthor numerical evaluations and similar-case arguments are retained without independent certification.
